subject: KiteMed trial: access, success criteria & credentialing plan
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@kitemed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: KiteMed trial: access, success criteria & credentialing plan

Hi Alex —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps for the 3‑week trial so we can get your engineering and security teams unblocked:

Scope we agreed on:
- Basic API integration to validate throughput and latency on a representative patient-messaging workload (approx 20–50k messages / 3 weeks).
- A short quality evaluation on 200 sample prompts across triage, appointment-scheduling, and messaging templates.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm/edit):
1) 95th percentile response latency <= 250ms for typical 64‑token completion workload
2) No SLA-affecting errors during 1k query window (target uptime 99%)
3) Qualitative accuracy: >= 85% pass rate on the 200 prompt eval set by KiteMed SMEs

Access & credentialing we need from KiteMed:
- API key creation: please indicate preferred scope. We recommend a trial key with read/write eval scope and a 3‑week expiry.
- IP allowlist: we'll provide our public egress ranges to whitelist (we also support SSO).
- SSO invite: if you want to gate the Redwood Console access, please add redwood-trial@kitemed.com to your Okta org (SAML).
- Sample data: a representative CSV (PII redacted) and the 200 prompt set for quality checks.

Owners & timelines (tentative):
- KiteMed SRE / Security to enable allowlist and SSO by Tue 21 Jul
- Redwood (Ben + Rafael) to provision trial keys and environment by Wed 22 Jul
- Kickoff run + eval: Thu 23 Jul — Fri 09 Aug (3 weeks)

Next steps: can you confirm SRE contact and procurement point of contact? Once we have that we’ll share the checklist and create the HubSpot plan.

Attachments: trial setup checklist and draft SLA (attached).

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

— Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

From: Alex Moreno <alex@kitemed.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@kitemed.com
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 15:31:00 -0400
Subject: Re: KiteMed trial: access, success criteria & credentialing plan

Thanks Naomi — good summary.

Confirming a few items from our side:
- SRE owner: Jordan Li (jordan.li@kitemed.com) — looping him in on the next email.
- Procurement: procurement@kitemed.com — they’ll need the PS summary and cost estimate for any overage beyond trial limits.
- Data: we can provide the 200 prompts and a sample CSV (deidentified). ETA for those assets: Mon 20 Jul.

On success criteria: 250ms 95th looks tight for our higher‑concatenation tests; can we note that we’ll evaluate both for short (<=64 token) and medium (<=256 token) path latency and set a soft target on the medium path?

We’d prefer the API key to be scoped to the evaluation environment only and rotated automatically at 3 weeks.

I’ll have Jordan coordinate allowlisting. If Redwood can send the exact IP ranges and SSO metadata, we’ll put that in the ticket.

— Alex
VP Product, KiteMed
alex@kitemed.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@kitemed.com>, Jordan Li <jordan.li@kitemed.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KiteMed trial: access, success criteria & credentialing plan

Appreciate the fast replies — hi Jordan, welcome.

Quick technical notes & what we’ll send today: 
- IP ranges for allowlist (egress / control plane): 34.82.91.10/32, 52.28.10.44/32, 52.28.10.45/32. If you prefer a CIDR block instead we can provide 34.82.91.0/24.
- SSO (SAML) metadata: attaching the metadata file and our ACS/Entity IDs. If you want us to do an IdP init flow instead we can trigger an invite once your org allows external SAML partners.
- API key: we’ll create an environment-scoped key with expiry set to 2026-08-09. Key will be marked 'trial-eval' and limited to 200k tokens total during the period.
- Sample payloads: we’ll include a set of 50 synthetic prompts that mirror the eval set (for integration smoke tests).

Security checklist we request you confirm in the ticket: SSO or SCIM needs, IP allowlist confirmed, any outbound log shipping allowed (S3/Webhook), and data retention window for logs (default 30 days during trial).

Attachments included: redwood-saml-metadata.xml, trial-ip-ranges.txt.

If all looks good Jordan — can you open the internal support ticket and paste the HubSpot trial ID? Naomi, I’ll add the environment and keys once Jordan confirms.

— Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | (510) 555-0123

Thanks everyone — quick confirmation from my side after Ben’s notes: 
- Jordan: please confirm the allowlist ETA (we can support staging first if you prefer) and whether you want SSO or token gating for Console access.
- Procurement: attaching the one‑pager PS estimate for any additional engineering support (no charge for the 3‑week baseline run).
- KiteMed success criteria: we’ll capture the two latency buckets in the evaluation doc and report both.

I’ve uploaded the trial checklist and draft SLA to the HubSpot record and Drive folder (links below). Once Jordan confirms allowlist and we get the sample data on Monday, Ben/Rafael will provision keys and environment and we’ll schedule a brief handoff call Wed 22 Jul 09:00 PT.

Best,
